next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Dates

glance_notes.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Dates
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The deadline to register to vote for Florida's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Dates
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Early Voting: The mandatory statewide early-voting period for Florida's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 24 through October 31. County Supervisors of Elections may offer additional early-voting days beginning as early as October 19 and ending as late as November 1.

glance_notes.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Vote-by-Mail
glance_notes.text: Vote-by-Mail Request Required: Florida does not automatically mail a ballot to every registered voter. A registered voter who wants to vote by mail must request a vote-by-mail ballot. No excuse is required.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Florida residents can register online through RegisterToVoteFlorida.gov, by mail or in person using the statewide voter registration application, through an office that issues Florida driver licenses or state identification cards, or through designated voter registration agencies. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be a Florida resident, and be at least 18 years old to vote; Florida allows preregistration beginning at age 16. A person who has been adjudicated mentally incapacitated with respect to voting cannot register unless voting rights have been restored. A person convicted of a felony must have voting rights restored under Florida law before registering or voting.
register.glance_value: Register online, by mail or in person
register.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Register to Vote or Update Your Information
register.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes registration methods and eligibility requirements. Additional verification source: 2026 Florida Statutes § 97.041 — [https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0000-0099%2F0097%2FSections%2F0097.041.html](https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0000-0099%2F0097%2FSections%2F0097.041.html) — establishes age, citizenship, Florida and county residence, mental-incapacity and felony requirements. Felony eligibility can depend on the offense and completion of sentence terms; official guidance: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/felon-voting-rights/](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/felon-voting-rights/). Individual felony eligibility should be determined through the official process rather than inferred by NSM.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Florida's official Voter Information Lookup to check your voter registration and party status. New registrations and updates may take one or two business days, and sometimes longer during registration-closing periods, to appear in the lookup. If you cannot find your information, contact your county Supervisor of Elections.
check_registration.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Voter Information Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: The official state lookup page directly establishes registration and party-status lookup, processing-time guidance and referral to the county Supervisor of Elections when information cannot be found.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Florida's voter registration deadline for an election is 29 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to register is October 5, 2026. Florida does not offer general Election Day voter registration, so an eligible person who is not registered by the applicable deadline generally cannot register and vote in that election.
deadlines.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Dates
deadlines.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes October 5, 2026 as the General Election registration deadline. Additional verification source: Florida Department of State Register to Vote or Update Your Information — [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/register-to-vote-or-update-your-information](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/register-to-vote-or-update-your-information) — establishes the general 29-day deadline. 2026 Florida Statutes § 97.055 governs registration-book closing. Florida law contains limited late-registration remedies for certain persons whose timely applications were not processed through specified agencies; the reader-facing statement therefore uses 'generally' rather than claiming there are no statutory exceptions.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: On Election Day, Florida voters must vote at the polling location assigned to their residential address. Use the Florida Division of Elections Voter Precinct Lookup to reach your county's official precinct and polling-place information, or contact your county Supervisor of Elections. Early voting is different: during early voting, a registered voter may use any designated early-voting site within the voter's county.
polling_place.glance_value: Election Day uses your assigned polling place
polling_place.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Day Voting
polling_place.internal_note: Primary source establishes assigned Election Day polling locations and directs voters to the official Voter Precinct Lookup. Supplemental source for countywide early-voting locations: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voting/early-voting-and-secure-ballot-intake-stations/](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voting/early-voting-and-secure-ballot-intake-stations/).

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Florida voters choosing to vote in person on Election Day must vote at their assigned precinct or polling location. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time. Anyone waiting in line at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote. Voters must present current and valid identification meeting Florida's photo and signature requirements. A voter who does not have acceptable identification may cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Day Voting
election_day.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes assigned-precinct voting, hours, the protection for voters waiting in line at 7:00 p.m., identification requirements and provisional voting when acceptable ID is not presented. The voter_id section documents the current 2026 identification list.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Florida polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time on Election Day. Any voter waiting in line at the polling place at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Election Day Voting
polling_hours.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly establishes 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. local time and confirms that voters waiting in line at closing may vote. The local-time wording matters because most of Florida is in the Eastern Time Zone while part of the Panhandle is in the Central Time Zone.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Florida requires early voting for elections that include a state or federal office. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, every county must offer early voting from October 24 through October 31. A county Supervisor of Elections may add optional days beginning as early as October 19 and ending as late as November 1. Each early-voting site must operate for at least 8 and no more than 12 hours per day during the applicable early-voting period. Registered voters may use any designated early-voting site within their county. Exact locations, optional dates and daily hours are set by the county Supervisor of Elections.
early_voting.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Early Voting and Secure Ballot Intake Stations
early_voting.internal_note: Primary source establishes statewide mandatory and optional periods, 8-to-12-hour daily range and countywide early-voting-site use. Election-specific verification: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates) — confirms October 24-31 as the mandatory 2026 General Election period. Supplemental statutory verification: 2026 Florida Statutes § 101.657 — [https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm/Ch0831/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.657.html](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm/Ch0831/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.657.html). The Division states that 2026 General Election site-specific information will be available after October 4, 2026, so reverify once those locations and schedules are published.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Florida voter may request a vote-by-mail ballot; no excuse is required. A request can be made through the voter's county Supervisor of Elections as permitted by Florida law. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to request that a ballot be mailed is 5:00 p.m. on October 22. A completed domestic vote-by-mail ballot generally must be received by the county Supervisor of Elections no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day to count; a postmark alone does not make an ordinary domestic ballot timely. Voters may return ballots by mail, in person to the Supervisor of Elections, or through an authorized secure ballot intake station when available. Vote-by-mail requests must periodically be renewed under Florida law.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; request by October 22
absentee_mail.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Vote-by-Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: Primary source establishes no-excuse vote-by-mail, request methods, the 5:00 p.m. 12th-day request deadline, return options, Election Day receipt requirement and request expiration rules. Election-specific verification: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates) — confirms October 22, 2026 as the deadline to request mailing. Supplemental statutory source: 2026 Florida Statutes § 101.62 — [https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.62.html](https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.62.html). Military and overseas voters have separate return rules addressed in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Florida voters voting in person must present current and valid picture identification. Under the 2026 law, accepted photo identification includes a Florida driver license; Florida identification card; U.S. passport or passport card; U.S. uniformed services or Merchant Marine identification; U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs veteran health identification card; Florida concealed-weapon or firearm license; or another identification card issued by a federal, state, county or municipal government entity, excluding identification cards issued by an educational institution. If the photo identification does not contain the voter's signature, an additional identification containing the voter's signature is required. A voter who does not present the required identification may cast a provisional ballot.
voter_id.glance_value: Current photo ID plus signature required
voter_id.source_name: 2026 Florida Statutes § 101.043 — Identification Required at Polls
voter_id.internal_note: IMPORTANT 2026 change: the current 2026 statute contains a narrower identification list than older Division of Elections guidance still visible online. Older guidance lists debit/credit cards, student IDs, retirement-center IDs, neighborhood-association IDs and public-assistance IDs. The 2026 codified statute directly establishes the current list and excludes educational-institution identification from the catch-all government-ID category. Because the official Division voter guidance appears stale relative to current codified law, the statute controls the claims presented here and this section should be reverified frequently for updated agency guidance or further legislative changes.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Florida requires voting methods to be accessible to voters with disabilities. Polling places must be accessible and usable by persons with disabilities, and at least one accessible voting system must be available at each polling place for early voting and Election Day. A voter may use accessible voting equipment to mark a ballot privately and independently or may receive voting assistance when permitted by law. Florida also provides accessible vote-by-mail options through county election officials for eligible voters with disabilities.
accessible_voting.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Accessible Voting for Persons with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes accessible polling places, accessible voting systems, independent voting and assistance options. It cites Florida Statutes §§ 101.715 and 101.051 and applicable federal accessibility requirements. Voters should contact their county Supervisor of Elections for the specific accessible vote-by-mail system and local assistance arrangements.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Florida provides special registration and vote-by-mail procedures for voters covered by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act. Covered voters include active-duty members of the U.S. uniformed services or Merchant Marine, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens residing outside the United States. These voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a vote-by-mail ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup when necessary. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Florida's deadline to transmit requested vote-by-mail ballots to UOCAVA voters is September 19, 2026. Special ballot-return rules apply to overseas voters, including an extended receipt period for qualifying ballots mailed from outside the United States.
military_overseas.glance_value: UOCAVA protections and federal forms available
military_overseas.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Military and Overseas Citizens Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes UOCAVA categories, FPCA registration/request options and special military/overseas procedures. Election-specific source: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates) — establishes September 19, 2026 as the UOCAVA transmission deadline. Florida law permits qualifying overseas ballots in a presidential-preference-primary or general election to be counted if postmarked or dated by Election Day and received within the statutory extended period. Because precise return rules depend on voter category and location, readers should follow the current UOCAVA instructions rather than applying the ordinary domestic vote-by-mail deadline.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students follow Florida's ordinary voting-residence rules. A student may register in Florida if Florida is the student's legal residence and the student otherwise meets Florida's voter qualifications. A student temporarily living away from a Florida voting residence while attending school can keep the Florida registration and use vote-by-mail or return to vote in the appropriate county. A student who moves to Florida and intends to make Florida the student's legal residence must register in Florida by the applicable registration deadline before voting here. Residence for tuition purposes is a separate legal issue and does not itself determine voter registration.
student_voting.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Register to Vote or Update Your Information
student_voting.internal_note: Primary source establishes Florida legal residence as a voter-registration qualification. Supplemental statutory source: 2026 Florida Statutes § 97.041 — [https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0000-0099%2F0097%2FSections%2F0097.041.html](https://leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0000-0099%2F0097%2FSections%2F0097.041.html). Section 101.045 separately recognizes electors temporarily residing outside their county while maintaining Florida and county residence: [https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.045.html](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0100-0199%2F0101%2FSections%2F0101.045.html). Florida's official election authority does not publish a current student-specific voter guide establishing a special student rule, so this section intentionally applies only the affirmative general residence rules and does not claim that college attendance by itself establishes Florida residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Florida sample ballots are provided through county Supervisors of Elections because the contests and ballot questions a voter sees depend on the voter's county, districts and precinct. Use the official state directory to reach your county Supervisor of Elections and obtain the correct sample ballot when it is available. County election offices also publish information about candidates and issues that will appear on the actual ballot.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Get your sample ballot from your county
sample_ballot.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — County Supervisors of Elections
sample_ballot.internal_note: Florida Division of Elections Candidate FAQ — [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/frequently-asked-questions/faq-candidates](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/frequently-asked-questions/faq-candidates) — expressly directs voters to county Supervisor of Elections websites and sample ballots for the candidates and issues appearing on the actual ballot. Florida has 67 county Supervisors of Elections, and the state directory was updated August 3, 2026. No single statewide voter-specific sample-ballot lookup was identified, so the county directory is the appropriate official reader-facing action link.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, R.A. Gray Building, Room 316, 500 South Bronough Street, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0250. Main phone: 850-245-6200. Voter Registration Services: 850-245-6290. Voter and Election Assistance Hotline: 1-866-308-6739, available Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time with extended hours during statewide elections. Florida Relay Service is available by dialing 711. For voter registration, early voting, polling locations and vote-by-mail questions specific to your county, contact your county Supervisor of Elections.
contact.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: Primary source directly verifies mailing address, main phone, Voter Registration Services phone, toll-free voter hotline, hotline hours and 711 relay service. The official page also publishes email addresses, but the web retrieval layer redacts them as protected email text, preventing direct verification of the literal address. No email address is therefore placed in reader-facing content rather than guessing. County contact directory: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/supervisor-of-elections](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/supervisor-of-elections).

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Florida Department of State, Division of Elections website for statewide election dates, voter-registration guidance, voting rules and official election resources. RegisterToVoteFlorida.gov is the state's online voter-registration system. Florida's 67 county Supervisors of Elections administer elections within their counties and provide local polling places, early-voting locations, vote-by-mail services and sample ballots. Some municipal clerks conduct local elections that are not held with county or statewide elections.
official_resources.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections
official_resources.internal_note: Official voter registration information: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voter-registration/). Official Voter Information Lookup: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/check-your-voter-status-and-polling-place/](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/check-your-voter-status-and-polling-place/). Official 2026 election dates: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates). Official voting information: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voting/](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voting/). Official county Supervisor directory: [https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/supervisor-of-elections](https://dos.fl.gov/elections/contacts/supervisor-of-elections). The county directory expressly states that Florida has 67 Supervisors of Elections and that some municipal clerks conduct their own local elections.
